body.estimand_functional: \(U(P)<+\infty\iff D_\infty(P)=\operatorname{dist}_\infty(P,\mathcal C_\infty)>0\), with the exact finite value obtained by certified feasibility over \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\)

sampling_model.design: One fixed, known cell with \(Y_0=h_0\), finite menus \(M_1,M_2\), and rational prices \(p\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent consumers drawn from the common cell distribution.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no randomized treatment; lagged choice is the state variable in the structural utility model.
sampling_model.overlap: No positive lower bound is imposed on any path probability; zero cells are included.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the \(m\)-cell path law \(P\) is estimated, by multinomial frequencies \(\widehat P\); latent laws are profiled out by exact compatibility. Inference fixes \(L_n=n\) and \(\eta_n=1/n\), uses rational primal--dual distance certificates, and tests the terminal response set separately from every finite price stratum and breakpoint.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Condition 2.2 and Theorem 2.3(a), PDF p. 20 of the canonical revised-July-2025 manuscript, require the two comparator subsets to coincide in a common choice universe and yield the adjacent-period joint probability inequality; the application excludes changing plan offerings.
Proposition 2.14 proves that conditional-iid probability bodies can be convex, closed, and nonpolyhedral, and Remark 3.9 shows that the Pakes inequalities are not sharp.
Theorem 1 on p. 7 proves that Algorithm 2's polynomial program is sharp; Section 5 on pp. 8--10 and Algorithm 3 give interruptible, progressively refined valid bounds and \(\varepsilon\)-sharpness.
The paper gives a necessary-and-sufficient random-utility cone representation and a uniformly valid test for stochastic rationalizability.
The paper pushes posterior uncertainty in a discrete-response PMF through a set-valued identification map and proves identified-set posterior consistency.

body.tldr: Within one known fixed design cell, the project represents conditional-iid turnover probabilities as the convex hull of a quadratic response-table map.  Strict comparison graphs yield finitely many rational price breakpoints, after which the compatible body is constant; separation from that terminal body is exactly the finite switching-cost-ceiling criterion for the maintained absolutely continuous subclass.  Exact finite semialgebraic feasibility recovers the frontier, and observable-moment compression gives certified finite-menu approximation and simultaneous multinomial inversion.  The constructive three-plan analysis currently covers positive-sign entry and two negative-sign boundary faces; the complete latent-free Boolean elimination for the remaining entry and exit classes remains \(\texttt{oeq:three-plan-analytic-body}\), not a claimed result.

project_justification.gap: Pakes et al. Condition 2.2 and Theorem 2.3(a), PDF p. 20 of the canonical revised-July-2025 manuscript, require the two comparator subsets to coincide in a common choice universe and deliver the resulting joint probability inequality. Entry or exit changes the feasible winner--loser comparisons and prevents that common-universe samplewise containment from covering the full observed menus. Mbakop's conditional-iid geometry shows that adding more linear inequalities cannot generally recover sharpness. No inspected paper gives an exact upper-tail saturation theorem, an observable finite-ceiling criterion, or a complete analytic three-plan turnover body.
project_justification.niche: Two observed post-initial choices are short enough that conditional iid becomes a quadratic mixture-of-products restriction, yet menu turnover makes this curved geometry economically consequential rather than a generic computation exercise.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the finite terminal comparison graph, represents each exact compatible body as the convex hull of a conditional-iid quadratic map, proves the observable finite-ceiling frontier, and recovers the exact identified set through finitely many rational price strata with certified semialgebraic feasibility.  It supplies constructive three-plan formulas for positive-sign entry and two informative negative-sign boundary faces while leaving the complete latent-free Boolean elimination as \(\texttt{oeq:three-plan-analytic-body}\).  For arbitrary finite menus, equal-moment compression and rational-grid linear programs provide a deterministic error bound and a uniformly covering inference layer.

body.related_work: Pakes, Porter, Shepard, and Calder-Wang motivate the fixed-effect and state-dependence problem. In the canonical revised-July-2025 NBER manuscript, Condition 2.2 and Theorem 2.3(a) on PDF p. 20 take two subsets of one common choice universe and, for adjacent periods, require those subsets to coincide. Condition 2.2 requires for every lagged choice in that common subset that the minimum structural-utility change among choices inside it dominate the maximum change among choices outside it. Theorem 2.3(a) then yields the primary joint inequality \(\Pr(Y_1\in A,Y_2\in A\mid Y_0=h_0)\ge\Pr(Y_1\in A\mid Y_0=h_0)^2\); its conditional-probability ratio form requires a positive denominator. With entry or exit, the common choice universe, available winner--loser comparisons, and complement differ across dates, so the samplewise containment preceding Jensen's inequality cannot directly cover the full changing menus; the application on PDF pp. 21--22 removes comparisons with different plan offerings and cannot use year pairs crossing 2011. Mbakop's Proposition 2.14, Theorem 3.6, Remark 3.9, and appendix construction are the closest identification method: response patches and mixture geometry are adapted, but the target here is a turnover-specific terminal frontier and explicit nonlinear projection. The maintained full-vector conditional Lebesgue absolute continuity condition is stronger than Mbakop's conditional continuity requirement and is used only to place smooth densities in strict open response patches for exact attainability. Duarte et al. Theorem 1 on p. 7 proves sharpness of Algorithm 2's polynomial program, while Section 5 on pp. 8--10 and Algorithm 3 supply interruptible, progressively refined valid bounds and \(\varepsilon\)-sharpness; those results motivate the general finite-menu fallback, not the three-plan analytic answer. Kitamura and Stoye provide the nearest frequentist probability-body testing precedent, although their random-utility cone is polyhedral and cross-sectional. Khan, Ponomareva, and Tamer characterize sharp dynamic binary sets under conditional stationarity, and Pakes and Porter establish sharp static multinomial fixed-effect inequalities; neither paper combines multinomial state dependence, changing menus, and conditional iid. Tamer and Walker occupy the generic Bayesian PMF-to-set inference rung, so inference here is deliberately limited to finite-sample frequentist coverage of the model-specific frontier. Polyakova supplies the downstream Medicare Part D use: switching-cost magnitudes enter risk-sorting and regulation counterfactuals, for which a nonparametric ceiling is a robustness restriction rather than a welfare-identification result.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The presolve reduces negative three-plan entry exactly to four pure rays and eight rank-one quadratic curves. Its dual support reduction couples the two off-diagonal path probabilities through a minimum multiplied by a positive-part expression. This coupling shows why separately optimizing corrected Jensen or boundary-face inequalities is not complete. The full active-allocation elimination for this joint regime, the zero-sign entry class, and all six exit classes is intentionally retained as \(\texttt{oeq:three-plan-analytic-body}\).
body.honest_scope: The result concerns one known two-choice design cell with stable plan quality, a common \(\kappa\), unrestricted fixed-effect mixing, conditional serial independence and time homogeneity, and conditionally iid shocks whose full-vector conditional laws are Lebesgue absolutely continuous.  Necessity uses the resulting fixed-cell sequential-exogeneity and stationarity factorization; constructive sufficiency uses the stronger open-patch absolute-continuity regularity.  Accordingly, the exact body is for the published fixed-cell class intersected with explicit no-tie and absolute-continuity conditions, not the whole broader published class.  A terminal rationalization constructed inside this subclass also proves nonidentification in any containing class, but failure to belong to the subclass terminal body does not by inclusion alone exclude rationalization in the larger class.  The note does not identify welfare, validate changing plan quality, impose monotonicity of \(\Theta(P)\), promise polynomial-time computation, claim a complete three-plan elimination, or claim uniform consistency when \(D_\infty(P)=0\).
